text.p: Grand Metropolitan Plc and Guinness Plc, the two British firms which announced merger plans on Monday, together have around $6.4 billion outstanding long-term bond issues, according to Reuter Fixed Income 3000 data.
The merger, to create GMG Brands, will bring together two firms whose experience in international bond markets has little overlap, thus complementing each other.
Analysts see GMG creating a similar synergy in the world drinks markets.

Reuters data showed GrandMet's bond portfolio to be the larger ($4.7 billion). The average bond was larger in size and longer in duration, mainly because of heavy issuance in the Yankee bond market where it has bonds stretching out to a maturity of 2035.

Guinness has more closely targeted European retail investors. Its longest-dated bond is a French franc issue due November 2002. Over half its $1.7 billion outstanding debt will mature before the millenium.

Both firms have debt in the medium-term note market.
GrandMet has nine outstanding deals worth $122 million and Guinness has 10 deals worth $1.1 billion (including some of the above, as noted), according to Webster MTN Service.
The merger between GrandMet and Guinness is worth more than 20 billion pounds ($32 billion). GMG Brands will be the world's seventh largest food and drinks firm.

The merger will also form the world's leading branded spirits and wine company with combined spirits sales of over 100 million cases a year, bringing together brands such as GrandMet's Smirnoff vodka and Cinzano with Guinness-owned Johnnie Walker whisky and Gordon's gin.
It also unites GrandMet's strong U.S. food interests through Burger King and Pillsbury with Guinness' brewing operations which include its famous stout ale.
